transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Michael Donovan (CISO, Gateway Trust), Sara Liu (Head of Cloud), Jamal Ortiz (SecOps), Emily Park (PM)

Auto-summary: weekly pilot security check-in; MC asked about SSO and audit log schema; Redwood to send SOC2 and network diagram; SE to enable audit logging in staging; customer to provide retention fields.

[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off the weekly security sync for the POC. quick roll call?
[00:06] Michael Donovan: michael here, C I S O at gateway trust, afternoon.
[00:09] Sara Liu: sara, head of cloud.
[00:11] Jamal Ortiz: jamal, sec ops.
[00:13] Emily Park: emily, pm on the pilot.
[00:15] Alex Morgan: great, and we have priya from my team, she'll be driving the SSO + logging work, and i'll own coordination and docs.
[00:22] Priya Kapoor: hi all, quick agenda: quick results review from the pilot, then SSO status, audit logs and retention, SOC2 evidence/questions, and then action items.
[00:30] Alex Morgan: sound good. priya, do you want to kick off with the short results review?
[00:33] Priya Kapoor: sure. so last week we ran the embedding and generation flows through the staging cluster with quantized model v2, average latency for 512 tokens was ~210ms p50 and p95 about 420ms when batching is enabled. we saw a bit higher tail when we hit cache misses - the K V cache warmup matters. note, our telemetry labels in the logs currently show service name as "Red wood-api" in some spans - that's an auto transcript artifact, ignore.
[00:57] Jamal Ortiz: when you say audit logs, are those the same traces i'm seeing in the console or are there separate raw audit exports we can ship to our SIEM?
[01:04] Priya Kapoor: good question. we have two things: the per-request trace in console for debugging and a structured audit export (json) that can be pushed to your S3, or streamed via syslog to your SIEM. the staging tenant we set up has audit logging turned on but we need to toggle the export to your bucket.
[01:20] Sara Liu: what's the retention on the audit logs in the pilot? can we set it to 90 days? also any PII concerns?
[01:27] Alex Morgan: by default pilot tenants retain logs for 30 days, but we can configure retention to your spec for the POC. we also support field-level redaction before export and encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed KMS for the exported artifacts.
[01:39] Michael Donovan: ok on KMS. we need to see the K M S integration details and an explanation of who has key access. is Redwood going to hold keys or are we bringing our own?
[01:47] Priya Kapoor: you can bring your own keys via KMS/HSM integrations in the private deployment and in dedicated we support KMS as well. for hosted POC we can do a customer-managed KMS with limited access - i'll attach the integration notes.
[01:57] Emily Park: we have a compliance checklist item: need to see SOC2 report and scope for the current hosted infra. can you share?
[02:03] Alex Morgan: yes, we'll share the SOC2 Type II for the past 12 months and the scope in the next couple days. i'll include a one-pager that maps SOC2 controls to the artifacts we can produce for audits.
[02:13] Jamal Ortiz: on SSO - we sent IdP metadata yesterday but haven't had a test in staging yet. what's blocking?
[02:19] Priya Kapoor: we got the metadata, thanks. blocked because we needed a test user and we had the staging tenant not peered to your VPC. once you share that test account and we enable the IdP in sandbox, we can run an end-to-end SAML login.
[02:31] Michael Donovan: we prefer SAML, not OIDC for now. also need SAML assertions to include role attribute for RBAC mapping. can Redwood map attributes to roles?
[02:39] Priya Kapoor: yes, we map attribute names to internal roles; you can pass role or groups. we'll send an example mapping and the exact attribute names we expect. small note - sometimes IdP metadata parsing gets slightly off in auto-import; if anything fails we'll accept the raw metadata file and import manually.
[02:55] Sara Liu: about audit schema: what fields are available? we're looking for user id, request id, model version, token counts, request payload hashes, and timestamp. also would like an event for KV cache miss/hit.
[03:06] Priya Kapoor: current audit export includes timestamp, request_id, user_id (if present), model_id and model_version, token_count, latencies, and a sha256 hash of the input payload if requested. we can include a kv_cache_event field that flags miss/hit in the trace. i'll confirm field names in the exported json schema.
[03:23] Alex Morgan: note that some of the field names in our console are snake_case and in export they may be camelCase depending on the SDK - little inconsistencies we've seen in prior pilots, just flag them and we'll normalize.
[03:33] Jamal Ortiz: for data retention and redaction, can we redact the entire input for specific request types, or only fields?
[03:38] Priya Kapoor: we support both. you can configure redaction rules by regex or by field name before we store or export. for the pilot we can enable a rule set that redacts account numbers and PII.
[03:51] Michael Donovan: encryption in transit and at rest - want to confirm TLS 1.2+ and SSE with customer-managed KMS for exports.
[03:58] Alex Morgan: yes, TLS 1.2+ enforced; we recommend TLS1.3. exports use SSE-KMS when you supply a key.
[04:05] Emily Park: is there an audit log for admin actions in Redwood console? we need to show who changed retention or who rotated keys.
[04:12] Priya Kapoor: yes we have an admin audit trail - it captures admin user, action, timestamp, IP, and a before/after snapshot for ACL changes. we can include that in the exported audit bundle for your compliance team.
[04:23] Sara Liu: can we request more retention for the admin audit trail vs request logs? like 365 days for admin and 90 days for request logs?
[04:29] Alex Morgan: yes, retention windows are configurable per-log-type; for longer retention we recommend exporting to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules for cold storage.
[04:37] Jamal Ortiz: about SOC2 - does Redwood publish a bridge letter for gaps if we need one during the pilot?
[04:43] Alex Morgan: we can provide a SOC2 attestation and a standard bridge letter for the period since the last audit - we'll include that in the packet.
[04:51] Michael Donovan: ok good. can you also outline any penetration testing allowances? we might want to run a non-disruptive pentest during the pilot.
[04:58] Priya Kapoor: we have a pentest policy; non-disruptive external scans are ok with prior notice. for more intrusive tests we coordinate with our security team and need a short approval window - i'll attach the pentest policy doc.
[05:08] Alex Morgan: quick note on private vs dedicated - if you need the keys never leaving your VPC, discuss private deployment, but for this POC we can emulate those controls with dedicated + customer-managed KMS.
[05:19] Sara Liu: on the topic of model variants and fallback - do logs include which model variant served the request if fallback happens? we want to attribute results to specific model hashes.
[05:28] Priya Kapoor: yes, model_version or model_hash is included in the audit record; if fallback occurs we log primary_model and fallback_model fields and reason for fallback.
[05:36] Emily Park: performance-wise, we saw some tail events. are there knobs we can use to reduce p95 without changing model?
[05:41] Priya Kapoor: yes: increase batch size, enable KV cache warmup, or route specific low-latency routes to dedicated capacity. for POC we can pin a small pool to reduce variability.
[05:52] Jamal Ortiz: for the SSO test we need to confirm SAML assertion attributes - i'll send a sample assertion payload.
[05:58] Alex Morgan: perfect. also, regarding audit exports to SIEM, do you prefer raw JSON or flattened CSV?
[06:03] Sara Liu: JSON is fine, SIEM can parse it. flattened CSV might lose nested fields like model metadata.
[06:10] Priya Kapoor: noted. we'll keep JSON.
[06:13] Michael Donovan: one more question: what parts of logs are redacted in hosted shared clusters? i understand you have multi-tenant infra; are customer inputs ever visible to other tenants?
[06:22] Alex Morgan: no cross-tenant visibility. tenant isolation at the service level is enforced; but for hosted we do use shared infra - inputs are logically isolated and access controlled. for higher assurance we recommend dedicated or private. we'll include an architecture diagram to show separation.
[06:36] Emily Park: on the timeline - we want to validate SSO and run a short benchmark before our steering committee on 2026-09-01. can we hit that?
[06:44] Alex Morgan: yes, if jamal shares metadata by 2026-08-14 we'll run SSO test by 2026-08-20 and benchmark week of 2026-08-24 which gives you results ahead of 9/1.
[06:53] Jamal Ortiz: i can get metadata and a test account today or tomorrow.
[06:56] Priya Kapoor: for the benchmark we'll enable KV cache and run the previously-agreed prompt set. expectation: we'll capture token counts, latencies, and audit export afterwards.
[07:06] Sara Liu: please include model version and quantization profile in the report so we can compare across runs.
[07:10] Priya Kapoor: will do.
[07:12] Michael Donovan: any regulatory concerns about PII in embeddings? we need clarity on whether embeddings contain reconstructable PII.
[07:20] Alex Morgan: embeddings are deterministic outputs; we can avoid storing raw inputs persistently if that's your preference - we can store only embeddings and hashed references, or redact sensitive fields prior to embedding. we'll add guidance in the artifact we send.
[07:33] Emily Park: ok thanks. can i get a short write-up for the steering committee that lists security controls, outstanding risks and mitigation?
[07:39] Alex Morgan: yes, we'll prepare a one-page risk/matters-of-note doc.
[07:42] Priya Kapoor: quick recap of open items: need Jamal's IdP metadata and test user; Alex to send SOC2 + network diagrams; Priya to enable audit export to customer's S3 in staging; Michael to share retention field list.
[07:55] Michael Donovan: correct. i'll add those to our tracker.
[08:00] Alex Morgan: any other questions?
[08:03] Sara Liu: none on my end.
[08:05] Jamal Ortiz: all good.
[08:07] Emily Park: no.
[08:09] Alex Morgan: great - thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the SSO test.
[08:13] Priya Kapoor: thanks, bye.

End of meeting
